newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia budget panel sets higher 97 deficit.
newsitem.headline: Russia budget panel sets higher 97 deficit.

text.p: The conciliation commission of government and parliamentary representatives working on Russia's 1997 draft budget agreed to raise the projected deficit, and said the difference would be mostly covered by increased foreign borrowing, commission members said on Friday.
The new deficit would be 95.4 trillion roubles or 3.5 percent of gross domestic product instead of the government's projected 90.7 trillion or 3.3 percent.
First deputy finance minister Vladimir Petrov said the government would increase foreign borrowing by four trillion roubles as a result.
It was not immediately clear whether the wider deficit was due to increased spending or lower revenues.
Parliamentarians had said the government's projections, already revised once, were based on unrealistic revenue assumptions.
The draft under discussion by the commission had provided for foreign borrowing of 41.22 trillion roubles in 1997 to cover a deficit of 90.70 trillion roubles.
It assumed revenues of 432.81 trillion roubles and spending of 523.51 trillion.
